transcript:
Header: Redwood Inference security review
Date: 2025-06-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Jae Kim (Redwood Solutions), Priya Nair (Acme CISO), Ethan Cole (Acme Head Platform), Diane Park (Acme Compliance), Marcus Lee (Acme DevOps)

Summary:
- Primary focus: data handling, prompt/content retention, PII/PHI handling, confirmation on training/no-training of customer data, KMS/encryption, SOC2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO and audit logging.
- Acme is healthcare vertical; major requirement: no customer data used to train public models, strict retention controls, KMS w/ customer-managed keys, audit logs retention 7+ years, and VPC/on-prem options.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, KMS integration docs and clarify retention controls and training guarantees.

Topics: SOC 2, ISO27001, RBAC/SSO, SAML, Audit logs, Data residency, KMS/HSM, Prompt retention, PII/PHI, "no training" assurances, Private deployment options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone thanks for carving out the time. quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, AE focused on regulated accounts, Lina is our SE, Jae is on solutions.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks. I'll kick off with why we're here. Acme Health handles PHI and lots of sensitive PII, so we need clarity on how Redwood handles prompts and outputs, and if customer data could be used to further train models.
[00:23] Lina: Totally, we saw that in the invite. We can walk through SOC 2 posture and how our platform handles data by default, plus options for private deployments and KMS.
[00:30] Ethan: Two quick asks up front: 1) confirmation that Redwood does not use our prompts or outputs to train or improve public models; 2) ability to hold all inference data in our VPC and manage keys.
[00:42] Samir: Short answer: yes on the private/control plane options, and we have contractual language around training on customer data, but we'll share the exact wording. For hosted API by default we retain logs for X days for troubleshooting unless you opt for dedicated/private where retention can be configured.
[00:58] Diane: When you say "contractual language" can you point to where that appears? We need something that can be reviewed by legal — a clause that says no training on customer data unless explicitly allowed.
[01:10] Samir: Absolutely. We'll send the standard DPA and a section in the customer agreement that addresses model training. It's in the security pack too, I'll include it in the next email.
[01:17] Marcus: On the KMS side, do you support customer-managed keys and an HSM flow? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[01:25] Lina: We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with BYOK integrations to major cloud KMS providers. For private deployments you can bring an HSM and we support CMK rotations. There's a few different flows; I'll share the diagrams.
[01:37] Priya: Audit logs — what's included? We need token-level tracing, who called what, request payload metadata, and retention for audit purposes (minimum 7 years).
[01:48] Jae: Our audit logs include request/response metadata, user identities proxied via SSO, model version and route, timestamp, latency. Full request payloads are configurable — by default we store minimal payloads for 30 days for debugging, but you can configure to store nothing or to ship logs directly to your splunk/siem via forwarder. Retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[02:06] Ethan: Can you confirm if the default hosted API ever stores full prompts or responses in a way that could be accessed internally?
[02:13] Lina: For hosted, we log traces for operational debugging and abuse monitoring. Full content storage is opt-in for customers; otherwise we keep hashes and metadata. Our internal access is restricted and audited — SOC 2 controls apply. But again, for PHI-heavy use, we recommend Private or Dedicated where you control storage.
[02:30] Priya: Okay, but we need an explicit "no training" statement for hosted as well — like the company does not use customer prompts to train models.
[02:37] Samir: Right. Redwood has a no-training-by-default policy for customer data on public models. I'll send the formal guarantee language. We also have a "no-derivative training" clause for Dedicated/Private customers unless they opt in.
[02:48] Diane: Are there any exceptions? For example, aggregate telemetry for safety improvements?
[02:53] Lina: We do collect telemetry for safety and operational improvements, but that's anonymized and aggregated. It doesn't include raw customer prompts for customers who opt-out. We'll include the telemetry policy in the pack.
[03:03] Marcus: Networking — we need to understand egress patterns. If we do a Private deployment, is any traffic routed through Redwood control plane in the cloud? Concern about metadata leakage.
[03:14] Jae: For Private options the control plane can be customer-hosted or a thin control plane with no payload routing. We'll provide network diagrams. The default hosted path obviously routes through Redwood, but payloads can be kept in-customer VPC with dedicated peering for Dedicated deployments.
[03:28] Ethan: Encryption at rest — do you support CMEK for the model KV caches and cache snapshots?
[03:35] Lina: Yes, CMEK for persistent storage. In-memory KV caches during inference are encrypted in transit and memory-protected; persistent snapshots encrypted with your CMK. We'll include the cryptography whitepaper.
[03:44] Priya: For compliance evidence, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? Are they current?
[03:51] Samir: We have SOC 2 Type II (most recent report 2025 Q1) and ISO 27001 certified for our control plane. We'll send redacted reports and an SSP summary.
[03:59] Diane: Redaction is fine, but we need the control mappings for our auditors — show where RBAC, key management, and incident response map to our controls.
[04:08] Samir: We'll include a control mapping matrix.
[04:10] Priya: One more on data residency: we need EU and US-only residency options and a statement on cross-border processing.
[04:17] Lina: We have regionally isolated deployments. Hosted model endpoints can be pinned to regions, and Dedicated customers can be in specific cloud regions with no cross-region replication unless you enable it. For Private, obviously you choose the data center. We'll document the cross-border policy.
[04:30] Ethan: Ok. On RBAC and SSO — we require SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained role controls integrated with our directory. Is that supported?
[04:39] Jae: Yes, SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC is customizable with roles and resource-level permissions. We'll share example role configs.
[04:48] Marcus: Any limits on audit log exports? We want a continuous streaming export to our SIEM.
[04:53] Lina: Export via event forwarder or push to your cloud storage/SIEM. For Dedicated/Private this is straightforward. For hosted we can set up streaming hooks — there are throughput considerations but it's supported.
[05:02] Priya: About prompt retention — we need to enforce data retention rules at the request level. Can we set TTLs per route so PHI prompts are auto-deleted after X days?
[05:12] Lina: Yes, we support per-route retention policies. You can set zero retention for routes that handle PHI and route them through Private or Dedicated with no retention and log-only hashes.
[05:22] Diane: If we set zero retention, does that impact debugging capability and SLA for incident investigation?
[05:28] Samir: It reduces our ability to debug at the content level — we can still do metadata-based troubleshooting. For deeper debugging we typically ask customers to enable a short retention window or share redacted examples. We'll note tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.
[05:40] Priya: PHI/PII detection — do you provide any automatic redaction or PII scrubbing built-in?
[05:47] Lina: We provide optional PII scrubbers and detectors as middleware. They can run client-side or as part of ingest. For highest assurance, we recommend running scrubbing in your network before sending tokens to us.
[05:58] Ethan: A practical question: could you point to contractual language about indemnity or liability in case of a exposure?
[06:04] Samir: Those are legal-level items. We'll include standard indemnity and liability limits in the DPA/contract pack, and our enterprise agreements are negotiable. We'll flag anything special for PHI use cases.
[06:14] Diane: What about employees access — how is privileged access controlled and audited?
[06:20] Jae: Privileged access uses just-in-time provisioning, MFA, and is audited in our SIEM. Access requests, approvals and sessions are logged. We can share an access control matrix.
[06:30] Priya: Can you confirm whether any training data sets include customer-supplied prompts (even as anonymized)? This is a major dealbreaker.
[06:38] Lina: To be explicit: Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs to train our public or internal models unless the customer explicitly opts in. We have this as a contractual guarantee. We also have processes to scrub telemetry used for safety which is aggregated only.
[06:52] Priya: Great. We'll require that clause in writing.
[06:58] Samir: Noted. We'll include the exact non-training clause and sample contract language.
[07:03] Marcus: For Private deployment, what's the upgrade path and how are security patches handled?
[07:09] Jae: We manage a signed artifacts pipeline. For Private deployments you can opt for either automatic updates (we push signed updates) or manual patching with signed packages. All updates are hashed and verified.
[07:19] Ethan: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of? e.g., cloud infra providers, monitoring vendors?
[07:24] Samir: We'll provide a subprocessors list — mostly cloud providers for Dedicated, monitoring and observability partners, and storage providers. All subcontractors are covered by our vendor risk management and contract flowdowns.
[07:36] Diane: Incident response — what SLAs and playbooks do you have? For a breach involving PHI we need clear RTOs and notification timelines.
[07:46] Lina: We have an incident response playbook mapped to NIST CSF; typical notification windows are 72 hours for incidents with impact, plus forensic reports as part of enterprise support. We'll include our IRP summary.
[07:58] Priya: Ok this has been helpful. one last thing: data subject requests — can customers request deletion and how does Redwood support that?
[08:06] Samir: For Hosted, we have DSR flows and APIs, but customers are ultimately responsible for initiating. For Dedicated/Private we can help automate deletion in the customer's environment. We'll include the DSR doc.
[08:18] Jae: Also note that for compliance we can provide audit exports and attestations for DSR handling.
[08:25] Priya: Thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[08:28] Samir: Recap: we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, control mapping, non-training contractual clause, KMS integration guide, retention and RBAC docs, and schedule the follow-up POC network/diagram session.
[08:40] Diane: That works. We'll prepare a list of PHI/PII examples and the flows that will be most sensitive and share before the follow-up.
[08:48] Marcus: I'll pull together our VPC constraints and egress policies.
[08:52] Ethan: We'll aim to make a go/no-go decision on a pilot in 2 weeks pending docs.
[08:58] Samir: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and set a calendar for the diagram review.
[09:04] Priya: Thanks all. bye.

Note: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, minor speaker overlaps). See attachments referenced: SOC2_redacted.pdf (sent), ISO_summary.pdf (sent), KMS_integration_slide_deck.pdf (to send), RBAC_examples.yaml (to send).
